record.title: No Name on the Work Roll
record.premise: A stranger sent up the river on an Owing barge gives the gang's cook their name and trade in the barge's hold, and is freed on the landing by a sour gang-master on an order from Vosh-Leera of Jal-Veesa.
record.foundation: Built from main-plot.md §5 quest 1 (passed by the owner, 2026-11-17) and §1. The game opens in the hold of the Owing barge moored at Ashgate Landing; the hold's door is locked. Okeeh, the gang's cook, asks the player's name (the "player's name set from a conversation" block: the stage after her line opens the game's own name entry) and their trade (a profession as in Morrowind: each answer sets a stage that raises five skills by five; one answer lets the player name their own five, one at a time, each pick a stage that raises that skill by five). When the trade is given the door is unlocked from outside. Dralin Uveran, the gang-master, speaks first on the landing (the quest's one speaks-first line), says the player's name was struck from his roll this morning on Vosh-Leera's order, and passes on her word: she will have work for the player if they bring her some Sithis' beard from Reed-Sill Weir (owner, 2026-11-18: one place at a time, the moss first, then Vosh-Leera). Before the player takes the road, Dralin offers one piece of gear that dead cutters left behind (owner, 2026-11-22): a two-handed warhammer, a sword, a bow with arrows and a knife, or a spell tome of Sparks, each given on the pick and the rest withdrawn; the player may go without. The pieces are Black Marsh flint, wood and bamboo from Here There Be Monsters: Curse of Cipactli, matched to Skyrim's iron tier (#89). The player's pack holds two lockpicks. MN02 starts on this quest's stage 90 and carries the markers on the weir's moss and on Vosh-Leera's door. The side quest What the Herald Sent is left out: the main quest only. Okeeh and Dralin first answer the line's shared topics Hist, Jal-Veesa and the Owing.

truth.when: four days before the game opens
truth.what: The player, a stranger with no kin in the marsh, was given months of the Owing for a debt and put on the barge with a new reed gang bound for Ashgate Landing. Nobody on the barge knows them.

truth.when: the night before the game opens
truth.what: The barge moored in the river pool below the camp. Dralin locked the new gang in the hold to sleep, as he does with every new gang until their names are on his roll.

Vosh-Leera, root-herald of Jal-Veesa, came down the road with an order that the stranger's months be struck from the roll. Dralin cannot refuse a root-herald. He struck the name and lost a cutter he had paid for. She did not say why, and went back to Jal-Veesa. (She acts for the Toh-Reel-Ka, who comb the gangs for strangers with no kin; the player learns that in MN02.)

Weeltul, Jal-Veesa's tree-minder, needs Sithis' beard, a grey moss that hangs on the woven weir at Reed-Sill Weir, to warm her sick tree's cooling egg-pool. Vosh-Leera, who chose the stranger off the barge's list, left word with Dralin that she will have work for the stranger if they bring the moss, for she gives work only to one who helps the tree-minder first.

truth.when: the seasons before the game opens
truth.what: Cutters who died of fever on the reed beds left their gear with Dralin, who keeps what nobody claimed, a flint-studded warhammer, a flint-edged sword, a bamboo bow with flint arrows and a flint knife, and a spell tome of Sparks one of them had carried up from Stormhold.

facts.claim: The player is in the hold of an Owing barge moored at Ashgate Landing, a reed-cutters' camp on the river west of Loriasel, in Black Marsh.
The Owing is the marsh's sentence: months of owed work in place of a cell. The gang is here to serve its months cutting reed.
The hold's door is locked from outside until the gang-master takes the new gang's names.
The player's name was struck from the gang-master's roll this morning, on an order brought by Vosh-Leera, the root-herald of Jal-Veesa: they owe no months and are free.
Vosh-Leera's house is in Jal-Veesa, a town up the road to the east, past Reed-Sill Weir.
Vosh-Leera will have work for the player if they bring her Sithis' beard, a grey moss hanging on the woven weir at Reed-Sill Weir, which is on the road to the town.

Dralin can spare one piece of what dead cutters left behind for the player's road, their pick of a flint-studded warhammer, a flint-edged sword, a bamboo bow with twenty flint arrows and a flint knife, or a spell tome of Sparks.
A Hist is a great thinking tree, the size of a tower, with pale grey bark, roots standing out of the water and a pool of eggs at its foot; every Argonian village is built round one.

stages.journalText: I woke in the hold of a barge among a gang of strangers. The door is locked. An Argonian woman named Okeeh is watching me. I should speak to her and find out where I am.

objectives.objectiveText: Speak to Okeeh in the barge's hold.

information.going: I am in a locked ship's hold with strangers and know nothing else.
information.next: Speak to Okeeh, the woman watching me.
information.ways: There is one way on, to talk to her. I carry two lockpicks, but the door has no lock I can pick.

carriers.know: I am locked in a hold with strangers
Okeeh is the one to speak to

stages.journalText: Okeeh told me where I am: the hold of an Owing barge moored at Ashgate Landing, a reed-cutters' camp in Black Marsh, where the gang cut reed for the months they owe. I gave her my name, and now she wants to know what my trade was. She says the door stays barred until the gang-master takes our names.

information.going: I am in the hold of an Owing barge at Ashgate Landing, a reed-cutters' camp in Black Marsh. The Owing is the marsh's sentence: months of owed work in place of a cell. The door stays locked until the gang-master takes the new gang's names.
information.next: Tell Okeeh what my trade was.
information.ways: Seven answers: warrior, hunter, thief, battlemage, healer, nightblade (each names the five skills it raises by five), or naming my own five skills one by one.

stages.journalText: Dralin Uveran, the Dunmer gang-master of Ashgate Landing, met me on the landing. He struck my name from his roll this morning, on an order brought by Vosh-Leera, the root-herald of Jal-Veesa, so I owe no months. He does not know why she wants me, and he is sour about it. He says she will have work for me if I bring her some Sithis' beard, a grey moss that hangs on the woven weir at Reed-Sill Weir, east up the road. Before I go, he offered me one thing from what dead cutters left behind: a Naga warhammer, a Naga sword, a bamboo bow with arrows and a flint knife, or a spell tome of Sparks. I should take my pick, or tell him I will manage without.

objectives.objectiveText: Take your pick of Dralin's gear, or tell him you will manage.

information.going: I am free of the Owing: Vosh-Leera, root-herald of Jal-Veesa, had my name struck from the roll. I do not know why. She will have work for me if I bring her Sithis' beard. Dralin offers me one piece of dead cutters' gear for the road.
information.next: Choose one of Dralin's four pieces of gear, or tell him I will manage; then the moss at Reed-Sill Weir.
information.ways: A choice of one: the warhammer (Two-Handed), the sword (One-Handed), the bow with arrows and a knife (Archery), or the tome of Sparks (Destruction); or none. Whichever I take, the others are gone.

topics.label: Where am I?
topics.intent: Okeeh. Tells: "You're in the hold of the work barge, moored at Ashgate Landing, a reed-cutters' camp on the river west of Loriasel. This is Black Marsh, the Argonians' country." The barge brought this gang up from the sea to serve the Owing: months of owed work given by the marsh in place of a cell, served here cutting reed for the mat-makers of Stormhold. She is Okeeh, the gang's cook. The door is locked from outside, as it is for every new gang, until the gang-master, a Dunmer named Dralin Uveran, takes their names onto his roll; it will not be long. She does not know the player's face, and asks their name (a question; its answer is topic.mn01-name). Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: My name? I'll tell you.
topics.intent: Okeeh. Tells: she listens and says the name back, so she can shout it at mealtimes. Does: sets stage 20, whose start opens the game's name entry; then she asks what the player did before the marsh caught them: "Every gang has a fighter, a hunter, a thief and someone who knows a poultice. What were you?" (a question; its answers are the seven trade topics). Checks: nothing.

topics.label: What do you mean, my trade?
topics.intent: Okeeh. Tells: what the player did before is what they will be good at here; she lists the answers she has heard and what each is good for: a warrior (One-Handed, Two-Handed, Block, Heavy Armor, Smithing), a hunter (Archery, Sneak, Light Armor, Alchemy, One-Handed), a thief (Sneak, Lockpicking, Pickpocket, Speech, Light Armor), a battlemage (Destruction, Alteration, Conjuration, One-Handed, Heavy Armor), a healer (Restoration, Alchemy, Illusion, Alteration, Speech), a nightblade (Illusion, Sneak, One-Handed, Destruction, Light Armor), or "none of those: name me your own five". Whatever the player says, those five come a little easier from today. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: I was a warrior.
topics.intent: Okeeh. Tells: then the player can carry a blade and a shield. As she says it, the bar lifts from the hold's door outside; she tells the player they can go out onto the landing now: the gang-master is out there and will want their name. Does: sets stage 31 (One-Handed, Two-Handed, Block, Heavy Armor and Smithing each raised by five; the door unbarred). Checks: nothing.

topics.label: What is the Owing?
topics.intent: Okeeh (and, by his own row, Dralin from stage 90). Tells: the Owing is the marsh's sentence. Black Marsh's own towns keep no jails; a debtor, a thief or a stranger who broke the peace is given months of owed work instead, and a broker sells those months to a gang-master like Dralin, who feeds the gang and works them until the months are served. Most of this gang owe six months or a year. Nobody counts a stranger's months kindly. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: What is the Owing?
topics.intent: Dralin. Tells: months of work owed instead of a cell; he buys them from the broker at Stormhold and his cutters work them off on the reed beds. The player's months were bought and are gone now, and that is his loss, not theirs. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: What is a Hist?
topics.intent: Okeeh, an Argonian. Tells: a Hist is one of the great trees of Black Marsh, and they think. A Hist is as tall as a tower, with pale grey bark and roots standing up out of the water, and a pool at its foot where the eggs lie among the roots. Every Argonian village is built round its own tree. On a hatchling's naming day it licks its tree's sap, and the sap shapes it for life; her own tree is far to the south, and she still dreams of it. All the trees are joined at the root, so what one knows the others can know. An Argonian with a hand on the bark can hear them. They are not just trees: if a village's tree dies, no egg in its pools will hatch again. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: What is a Hist?
topics.intent: Dralin, a Dunmer. Tells: the Argonians' great trees, grey-barked and as big as towers, with an egg-pool at the foot; every village stands round one, and they say the trees think. He has seen men stand with a hand on one for an hour. Jal-Veesa's is the tall grey tree in the pool at the middle of the town, and it has looked poorly since the rains. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: What is Jal-Veesa?
topics.intent: Okeeh. Tells: the town of the Veesa-Teeleel, the Sedge-Wardens, east up the road: stilt houses on mud banks round its Hist, a lane down to the jetty on the creek, nets and fish drying on racks. The tall grey tree on its mound at the middle of the town is its Hist. She buys the gang's dried fish there. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: What is Jal-Veesa?
topics.intent: Dralin. Tells: the Sedge-Wardens' town, east up the road past Reed-Sill Weir: stilt houses round a pool with their Hist in the middle. Its elders answer to nobody in Stormhold, and its root-herald, Vosh-Leera, speaks for them to outsiders. Her house is in the town; any warden will point to it. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: Who are you?
topics.intent: Okeeh. Tells: the gang's cook; she owes no months, she is paid, and she has cooked for Dralin's gangs four seasons. She sells dried fish and lamp oil from her stall by the hut. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: Who are you?
topics.intent: Hara-Jeel. Tells: a reed-cutter of this gang, owing a year for a debt at Stormhold; he came up on the barge beside the player and does not know them either. The door opens when the gang-master wants it to. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: (speaks first) You. Off the barge.
topics.intent: Dralin Uveran, a step from the hold's door as the player comes out. Tells: he is Dralin Uveran, gang-master here. The player's name is not on his roll: he struck it this morning, before they cut a single reed, on an order brought down the road by Vosh-Leera, the root-herald of Jal-Veesa, the one who speaks for that town's elders and its tree to outsiders. He cannot refuse a root-herald. "You must have friends in high places." He paid for the player's months and has lost them. Vosh-Leera left word: she will have work for the player if they bring her some Sithis' beard, a grey moss that hangs on the woven weir at Reed-Sill Weir, the weir-wardens' camp where the road east meets the creek; her house is in Jal-Veesa, a little further on past the weir. What she wants with either of them he does not know and does not care to. Mind the crocodiles under the weir. Then: the player will need to look after themselves on the road. He has not got much to spare, but he can offer one of these, things dead cutters left behind when the fever took them: a Naga warhammer, flint set in a wooden head; a Naga sword, a wooden blade edged with flint; a bamboo bow with twenty flint-tipped arrows and a flint knife; or a spell tome of Sparks that one of them carried up from Stormhold, which teaches a lightning spell. Take your pick. Does: sets stage 50. Checks: nothing.

topics.label: I'll take the warhammer.
topics.intent: Dralin. Tells: he hands over the Naga warhammer, which the Naga call a cuauololli; it is heavy, and the flint will crack a crocodile's skull if the arm behind it is strong. He puts the rest away. Does: sets stage 51, which gives the Naga Cuauololli. Checks: nothing.

topics.label: I'll take the sword.
topics.intent: Dralin. Tells: he hands over the Naga sword, a macana in their tongue; keep the flint edge off stone, it chips. He puts the rest away. Does: sets stage 52, which gives the Naga Macana. Checks: nothing.

topics.label: I'll take the bow and the knife.
topics.intent: Dralin. Tells: he hands over the bamboo bow, twenty flint-tipped arrows (yaomitl, the Naga say) and the flint knife (a tecpatl); the arrows will not last, so pick them up after. He puts the rest away. Does: sets stage 53, which gives the Bamboo Bow, twenty Naga Yaomitl and the Naga Tecpatl. Checks: nothing.

topics.label: I'll take the spell tome.
topics.intent: Dralin. Tells: he hands over the tome of Sparks; he never read it, and better the player than the damp. He puts the rest away. Does: sets stage 54, which gives the Spell Tome: Sparks. Checks: nothing.

topics.label: I'll manage without.
topics.intent: Dralin. Tells: suit yourself; he puts the gear away. The road east is the road to the weir. Does: sets stage 90, which gives nothing. Checks: nothing.

topics.label: Who are you?
topics.intent: Dralin. Tells: the gang-master of Ashgate Landing, a Dunmer of Stormhold who buys Owing months and works them off on the reed. He has nothing more for the player. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: Who is Vosh-Leera?
topics.intent: Dralin. Tells: Jal-Veesa's root-herald. A root-herald speaks for a town's elders and its tree to anyone from outside, so an order from her is the town's order. She walked down this morning, gave the order and went back. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: What is Sithis' beard?
topics.intent: Dralin. Tells: a long grey moss that hangs on the woven weir at Reed-Sill Weir, the first camp on the road east. Tree-minders use it for something; why Vosh-Leera wants it he does not know. There are crocodiles under the weir where the wardens throw their offal; kill them, shoot them from the log walk on top of the weir, or keep out of their sight. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

state.name: Wanderer
state.notes: I am Wanderer, a hunter, now free of the Owing (reed-cutting service) at Ashgate Landing, Black Marsh. Dralin Uveran, the Dunmer gang-master, struck my name on orders from Vosh-Leera, root-herald of Jal-Veesa, who speaks for the town elders and tree. I carry a bamboo bow, 20 flint arrows (pick them up after use), a flint knife, 2 lockpicks, 0 gold. Next: go east up the road to Reed-Sill Weir, the weir-wardens camp, pick grey Sithis beard moss from the woven weir (watch for crocodiles under it), then take it to Vosh-Leera house in Jal-Veesa. Unknown: why she wants me, what a Hist is, and what Jal-Veesa tree is. Okeeh the cook is in the barge hold and Dralin is on the landing if you want to ask them more.
